result.side_resistance_note: Per-layer side resistance. 'method' gives the mobilized coefficient (alpha=... for cohesive, beta=... for cohesionless, rock socket); 'fs_kPa' is the unit side resistance. effective_top_m/effective_bottom_m reflect the zones that carry no side resistance: the top zone or the casing (unless top_exclusion is given, the top 1.5 m in cohesive soil and none in cohesionless soil or rock) and, where bottom_exclusion is given, that much above the base in cohesive soil. Under the GEC-10 (2018) beta, 'beta_steps' gives each cohesionless layer's phi', sigma'p, OCR, Ko, Kp, K/Ko and beta; 'alpha_steps' each cohesive layer's su, the su the alpha used (su(CIUC) under GEC-10's Eq. 10-18), su/pa and alpha.

choices.chosen: GEC-10 (2018) beta, Eq. 10-13, on each layer's average sigma'v: Q_s in cohesionless soil 1,553 kN, Q_ult 3,719 kN
choices.basis: GEC-10 (FHWA-NHI-18-024) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Step 5 of the design for axial load (Sec. 10.3), pp. 10-10 to 10-12: R_SN = pi B dz f_SN with f_SN = beta sigma'v (Eqs. 10-5, 10-7), sigma'v the 'average vertical effective stress over the depth interval' dz, taken here over each layer (Table 10-1, p. 10-6; Example 10-1 takes it at mid-layer). beta = K tan(delta) (Eq. 10-6) with delta = phi'; K = Ko, 'a rational first-order approximation' (K/Ko = 1, p. 10-11); Ko = (1 - sin phi') OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp = tan^2(45 + phi'/2) (Eqs. 10-8, 10-10; Mayne and Kulhawy 1982); OCR = sigma'p / sigma'v (Eq. 10-9) with sigma'p from N60 by Eq. 10-11 or 10-12; together Eq. 10-13. 'The value of beta at shallow depths should be limited to the value corresponding to a depth of 7.5 ft' (pp. 10-11, 10-12). phi' is the layer's where given, else 27.5 + 9.2 log (N1)60 (Example 10-1, p. 10-13; Appendix A, Eq. A-2, p. A-8). GEC-10 prints no upper limit on f_SN in cohesionless soil. Resistance factor 0.55 (p. 10-12)
alternatives: each layer split into sub-layers of 0.1 m, each on its own sigma'v (GEC-10 p. 10-7 splits a layer where its N-values vary by more than a COV of 45 %): Q_s in cohesionless soil 1,549 kN, Q_ult 3,715 kN

beta_method 'depth', O'Neill and Reese (1999) beta = 1.5 - 0.135 sqrt(z, ft), 0.25 to 1.2 (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print: Q_s in cohesionless soil 2,015 kN, Q_ult 4,181 kN

choices.what: K/Ko in cohesionless soil (construction's effect on the horizontal stress)
choices.basis: GEC-10 (FHWA-NHI-18-024) p. 10-11: 'A rational first-order approximation is that K/Ko = 1, assuming there is no stress change induced by construction'; p. 10-12: valid 'for dry, slurry (wet-hole), and casing methods of construction with minimal sidewall disturbance, proper handling of slurry and casing, and prompt placement of concrete'; 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly, the coefficient K can be reduced to 2/3 of its initial in-situ value (Ko), or lower if soil caving is allowed to occur. Judgment and understanding of the influence of construction activities are therefore needed'
alternatives: 2/3, where construction quality is not controlled properly (p. 10-12): Q_s in cohesionless soil 1,035 kN, Q_ult 3,201 kN

choices.what: preconsolidation stress sigma'p of cohesionless soil from N60
choices.chosen: Eq. 10-11, sigma'p/pa = 0.47 N60^m with m = 0.6 (clean quartzitic sands): 8-15 m
choices.basis: GEC-10 (FHWA-NHI-18-024) p. 10-11: Eq. 10-11, sigma'p/pa = 0.47 (N60)^m, 'where m = 0.6 for clean quartzitic sands and m = 0.8 for silty sands to sandy silts (e.g., Piedmont residual soils)' (Mayne 2007); Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15 N60, which 'Kulhawy and Chen (2007) suggest ... provides a good fit for gravelly soils'; 'sigma'p is estimated by Equation 10-11 for sandy soils and Equation 10-12 for gravelly soils'. The soil's description decides which; Example 10-1's silty sands take m = 0.8
alternatives: sigma_p_correlation 'silty_sand' on these layers, Eq. 10-11, sigma'p/pa = 0.47 N60^m with m = 0.8 (silty sands to sandy silts): Q_s in cohesionless soil 2,271 kN, Q_ult 4,437 kN
sigma_p_correlation 'gravel' on these layers, Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15 N60 (gravelly soils): Q_s in cohesionless soil 1,754 kN, Q_ult 3,920 kN

choices.chosen: GEC-10 (2018) alpha, Eq. 10-18, on su(CIUC) (1.5-8 m: su/pa 0.74, alpha 0.530): Q_s in cohesive soil 811 kN, Q_ult 3,719 kN
choices.basis: GEC-10 (FHWA-NHI-18-024) Sec. 10.3.5.2, Step 5 of the design for axial load, pp. 10-15 to 10-18: R_SN = pi B dz alpha su (Eq. 10-15); alpha = 0.30 + 0.17 / (su(CIUC) / pa) (Eq. 10-18, p. 10-16; Chen et al. 2011, Fig. 10-6, p. 10-17), 'recommended as a revision to the expressions for alpha currently given in the AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications (2017a)'; f_SN = alpha su(CIUC) (Example 10-2, p. 10-18). su is each layer's, with sigma'vo for a transform at the middle of the length that carries side resistance. Resistance factor 0.45 (Table 8-4, p. 8-14)
alternatives: alpha_method 'aashto', O'Neill and Reese (1999) as FHWA NHI-06-089 prints it (Eqs. 9-37a, 9-37b, p. 9-129), alpha = 0.55 for su/pa <= 1.5: Q_s in cohesive soil 842 kN, Q_ult 3,750 kN

choices.what: strength su in Eq. 10-18 (the test each cu came from)
choices.chosen: each layer's cu taken as su(CIUC), untransformed
choices.basis: GEC-10 (FHWA-NHI-18-024) p. 10-16: Eq. 10-18 is fitted to su(CIUC) (Fig. 10-6); 'For values of undrained shear strength determined by UC or UU lab tests, the value of su should first be transformed to its equivalent CIUC value' by Eq. 10-16 (UC) or Eq. 10-17 (UU), Chen and Kulhawy (1993), on sigma'vo at the layer's middle (Example 10-2, p. 10-18). Which test each cu came from is the engineer's to state: left out, cu is taken as su(CIUC), untransformed
alternatives: su_test_type 'uc', UC, transformed to su(CIUC) by Eq. 10-16: Q_s in cohesive soil 872 kN, Q_ult 3,779 kN
su_test_type 'uu', UU, transformed to su(CIUC) by Eq. 10-17: Q_s in cohesive soil 861 kN, Q_ult 3,769 kN

defaults_used.top_exclusion: 1.5 m in cohesive soil, 0 in cohesionless soil and rock: GEC-10 (FHWA-NHI-18-024) p. 10-17 prints the top 5 ft in Sec. 10.3.5.2, Cohesive Soils; Secs. 10.3.5.1 and 10.3.5.3 print no such zone in cohesionless soil or rock: Examples 10-1 and 10-5 take the sand's side resistance from the ground surface, Example 10-4 the socket's over its whole length

result.neutral_plane_basis: UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 procedure: the neutral plane is where the load curve (Q_dead + negative skin friction) meets the resistance curve (toe resistance + positive skin friction), with side and base resistance fully mobilized (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 steps 3-5, Fig 6-26). Unit skin friction (beta layers) and the toe in sand use the final effective stress, sigma'v0 plus the fill / drawdown change (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2). The pile's own weight is left out of the load curve, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 do (include_pile_weight=False).
result.methods_range: The methods give neutral planes from 5.99 m to 17.66 m and drag forces from 226 kN to 1308 kN (5 of 7 methods apply).
warnings: The neutral plane where the load and resistance curves intersect (17.66 m) lies below 5.99 m, where the computed soil settlement falls to the pile's; the friction between them is counted as negative although that soil settles less than the pile. With full mobilization that is UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4's conservative assumption for the drag force. For settlement, full base mobilization is not conservative (§6-5.8.4.2): see the 50% and 0% toe mobilization rows (toe_mobilization).

The soil below the pile toe has no compressibility in this model (18.00-20.00 m (cohesionless)), so its settlement counts as zero (here 0.0 mm below the toe in all). The toe load counts down to 18.86 m, where its stress increase falls below 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, p. 449): extend the profile at least that deep. The fill / drawdown stress increase does not decay with depth: give the profile down to the base of the compressible soil. Give Cc and e0 (or C_ec) for clay, or E_s for sand, to include it, and mark a layer settling if the fill / drawdown compresses it (UFC 3-220-20 Eqs 6-49 to 6-54, the equivalent footing at the toe).

FHWA GEC-12 Vol I §7.3.5.6 step 1c (p. 332) takes the settlement below the toe to 25.70 m, below the bottom of the soil profile (20.00 m), so the UFC 3-220-20 and FHWA GEC-12 depths were compared only to the bottom of the profile: pile head settlement 0.7 mm by UFC 3-220-20's and at least 0.7 mm by FHWA GEC-12's. Give the soil profile down to 25.70 m to compare them.

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at 100% toe mobilization
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Intersection of the load and resistance curves with side and base resistance fully mobilized: UFC §6-7.4 step 3 calls it 'a conservative approach for evaluating the drag force'; not conservative for settlement (§6-5.8.4.2).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at 50% toe mobilization
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Intersection of the load and resistance curves, side fully mobilized, toe at 50% of its nominal resistance: UFC §6-5.8.4.2 and GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 analyse 0%, 50% and 100% (Siegel et al. 2013).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at 0% toe mobilization
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Intersection of the load and resistance curves, side fully mobilized, toe at 0% of its nominal resistance: UFC §6-5.8.4.2 and GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 analyse 0%, 50% and 100% (Siegel et al. 2013).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Mobilized toe resistance compatible with the toe penetration
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Pile and soil settle equally at the neutral plane (Fig 6-19). The toe force follows the toe penetration: bearing-stratum compression under the toe force (UFC Eqs 6-51 to 6-54) standing in for a q-z curve, capped at the toe resistance; side fully mobilized.

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at the bearing layer (end-bearing pile)
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: UFC §6-7.4 step 5: 'the neutral plane will be located near the interface of the column and the bearing layer for an end-bearing column bearing in a stratum that is much stiffer than the compressible soil'. Plane at the base of the settling soil; set by that statement, not computed.

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at the pile toe
neutral_plane_comparison.source: FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.5.7 (p. 336; Goudreault and Fellenius 1994); CGPR #56 Table 3.1 'end bearing'
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: The whole shaft in negative skin friction: the upper bound on the drag force for a single pile. GEC-12 §7.3.5.7 uses the plane at the toe for group settlement.
neutral_plane_comparison.reason: with the neutral plane at the toe (18.00 m) the toe would have to carry 1751 kN, more than its resistance (1665 kN): the load and resistance curves put the plane higher.

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Endo et al. (1969)
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Neutral plane assumed at a fraction of the embedment; an estimate.

result.pile_weight_basis: Pile's own weight left out of the load curve, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 do

below_toe.criterion: 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, p. 449)
below_toe.basis: Below the toe (18.00 m) the toe force (1665.2 kN) is spread 2V:1H from an equivalent footing 0.40 m square at the toe (UFC 3-220-20 Eqs 6-49 to 6-52) and counted 0.86 m below the toe, to 18.86 m, where its stress increase falls below 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, p. 449). The fill / drawdown stress increase does not decay with depth, but no layer between the toe and the bottom of the soil profile (20.00 m) is marked settling, so it adds no settlement there. With 10% of the existing vertical effective stress instead (FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.5.6 step 1c, p. 332; influence_depth_criterion='effective_stress') the toe force is counted to the bottom of the soil profile, 20.00 m, short of 25.70 m, where its stress increase would fall below that: the same settlement below the toe, 0.0 mm.

other_criterion.criterion: 10% of the existing vertical effective stress (FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.5.6 step 1c, p. 332)

choices.what: depth to which the settlement below the toe is computed
choices.chosen: 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, p. 449)
choices.basis: The module's default, as the module follows UFC 3-220-20's procedure by default. The other rule's results are reported beside it (below_toe, other_criterion).
alternatives: 10% of the existing vertical effective stress (FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.5.6 step 1c, p. 332)

choices.what: difference between the UFC 3-220-20 and FHWA GEC-12 results that is warned about
choices.chosen: pile head settlements or drag forces more than 25 % apart: of the larger of the two
choices.basis: The engineer's call, not a reference's figure: neither UFC 3-220-20 nor FHWA GEC-12 says how far two settlement estimates may differ before it matters (the default, 25 %, is a round figure). A check that passes with one rule and fails with the other is always warned about; the rule used is not changed.

choices.chosen: Nt 60.0 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17, p. 421, Fellenius (2021) column = GEC-12 Table 7-9; sand, phi' 34 deg)
choices.basis: The module's default. The ultimate toe resistance, qb = Nq sigma'zD (UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-20; GEC-12 Eq. 7-20 with Table 7-9 for its beta method, p. 258), sigma'v final (skin_friction_stress); the drag procedures leave the method to the engineer (UFC §6-7.4 step 2; GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 Step 2).
alternatives: Nt 39.0 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17, p. 421, Cheng (2004) equation; phi' 34 deg, Z/b 45.0): Nt_method 'cheng'
Nt given: local experience (GEC-12 Step 5a) or a mobilized value

choices.what: skin friction method in the cohesive soil, 0-6 m
choices.chosen: Alpha method, fs = alpha x cu (UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-8)
choices.basis: The module's default for cohesive soil: undrained, short-term conditions (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.4.2, p. 414, and p. 410), as in UFC's drag force example (App. B-5.4, p. 636); FHWA recommends the α-method in cohesive soils (GEC-12 §7.2.1.2, p. 229). Either serves the drag procedures: 'an appropriate static analysis method' (GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 Step 2, p. 342); higher alpha and beta are conservative for negative skin friction (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2, p. 476).
alternatives: Beta method, fs = beta x sigma'v (UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-7), for long-term, drained conditions (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.4.1, p. 411; FHWA GEC-12 §7.2.1.3.4, p. 255): skin_friction_method 'beta' with beta (GEC-12 Table 7-9, p. 256: clay 0.15-0.35)

choices.what: beta in the cohesionless soil, 6-18 m
choices.basis: The module's default: GEC-12 Table 7-9 (p. 256; Step 2b, p. 257), the pairs UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-15 prints for driven piles (p. 414), by soil_class (sand unless given), linear in phi' and held at the range's ends. Higher beta is conservative for drag, lower for resistance (UFC §6-7.4 step 2, p. 476).
alternatives: beta given: local experience (GEC-12 Step 2a), or UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-6, K tan delta (Fig 6-13, Table 6-14)

choices.what: alpha in the cohesive soil, 0-6 m
choices.basis: The module's default, as the module follows UFC 3-220-20's procedure by default. UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.4.2 (pp. 415-417): alpha 1 in soft clay (su below 800 psf, Table 6-16); in firm to very stiff clay Fig 6-14, curve A for Z of 40b or more and curve B for Z = 10b, Z from the ground surface to the clay's base or the pile toe and b the pile width. UFC's drag example reads it so (App. B-5.4, pp. 636-637: alpha 1.0 in soft clay, 0.5 in stiff clay, Eq 6-9 in the transition zone).
alternatives: FHWA GEC-12 Fig. 7-17 (Tomlinson 1979): alpha_chart 'gec12_fig_7_17' with fig_7_17_curve; Ca by su, D/b and pile type, as drawn (GEC-12 §7.2.1.3.2 Step 1, p. 250)
alpha given on the layer; a higher alpha is conservative for negative skin friction, a lower one for resistance (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2, p. 476)

defaults_used.pile_perimeter: pi D, from pile_diameter: the perimeter of a circular section
defaults_used.pile_area: pi D^2 / 4, from pile_diameter: the solid circle; give the steel area for an H or pipe pile
defaults_used.Nt: the ultimate value from the toe layer: 9 in clay, else UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17 (Nt_method): the ultimate, not the mobilized, toe resistance
defaults_used.ground_elevation: no elevation: the figures plot depth below the ground and say no elevation was given; results are in depth either way

notes: Pressure above the excavation: sand apparent envelope (max 31.20 kPa) + surcharge 4.00 kPa (GEC-4 5.2.4 adds surcharge and water explicitly).
The bottom span's load is assigned wholly to the lowest support; free earth support gives that support 72.7 kN/m from the wall below it.
Embedment: free earth support about the lowest support, MR = FS x MD with FS = 1.5 (Caltrans T&S 8-4 uses 1.3).

warnings: A toe circle governs: the circle through the toe at (x = 10.00, z = 0.00) and the ground at x = 27.45 gives FOS 1.582, below the circular (search) minimum (1.587). The main search's entry/exit windows, centre grid or grid spacing kept it from this circle; the toe circle is reported.
The critical surface's entry point (x = 10.00) lies on the edge of the given x_entry_range (10.00 to 20.00); a lower factor of safety may lie outside it. Widen the range to check.
